No, according to [[write-journal]], it does not use a database transaction for rollback. The page explicitly states:

> "This approach gives each run all-or-nothing semantics for its writes **without needing a database transaction** — the in-process journal itself provides transactional guarantees."

Instead, the rollback mechanism relies on an **in-memory write journal** that records the prior state of files before any write occurs. On failure, the journal simply rolls back every recorded write in reverse order by restoring previous file content or deleting newly created files — all happening in memory during the agent run, without involving any database.
